communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Detroit scattered-site LIHTC developments
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Michigan State Housing Development Authority
FOIA Coordinator

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, MCL 15.231 et seq., I request electronic records concerning a group of Detroit Low-Income Housing Tax Credit developments constructed as scattered-site housing around the late 1990s and 2000s:

- Brewer Park Homes
- Creekside Homes
- St. John Homes
- Ephesus Homes
- Saratoga Homes
- Brightmoor Homes
- Nortown Homes I & II

For each project, please provide any record...

- Describing the project's intended long-term ownership or disposition strategy.
- Any record referring to tenant homeownership, lease-purchase arrangements, sale of individual homes to occupants or any commitment to make units available for purchase by tenants.

Additionally, please provide the following records for the above developments, grouped by type.

1. LIHTC dates and restrictions

- IRS Forms 8609 and any attached schedules in MSHDA's possession.
- Carryover allocation documents, placed-in-service records and records establishing the first year of the project's credit period.
- The project's recorded regulatory agreement, extended-use agreement, land-use restriction agreement or equivalent affordability covenant, including amendments.
- Any document identifying: the beginning and ending date of the 15-year compliance period; the beginning and ending date of the extended-use period; any additional affordability period imposed by MSHDA or another funding source.

2. Ownership and investor structure

- The original ownership or partnership organizational documents submitted to MSHDA, including partnership agreements or operating agreements if maintained in the project file.
- Records identifying the original developer, general partner or managing member, limited partner/investor member and syndicator.
- Records describing any anticipated investor exit after Year 15.
- Records showing amendments to those arrangements.

3. Transfers and dispositions

Records concerning the transfer of...

- the project;
- the ownership entity;
- the general-partner or managing-member interest;
- the investor interest; or
- individual houses or parcels.

For projects in which individual homes were removed from the LIHTC development or sold separately, please provide records identifying the address, date and nature of the disposition.

4. Compliance and physical condition 

- Annual owner certifications submitted during the most recent 10 years available.
- MSHDA physical inspection reports and tenant-file review reports during the same period.
- Notices of noncompliance, cure notices, corrective-action plans and records documenting whether cited deficiencies were corrected.
- IRS Forms 8823 submitted by MSHDA concerning the developments.
- Records concerning any failure to maintain required tenant, rent, occupancy or compliance records.

5. Financial condition

Please provide financial records maintained by MSHDA that reflect project-level operations, including:

- original development budgets and sources-and-uses statements;
- annual operating budgets;
- audited or unaudited financial statements submitted to MSHDA;
- rent rolls;
- replacement-reserve reports;
- requests to withdraw or use reserve funds;
- workout agreements;
- records identifying delinquent mortgage or MSHDA debt;
- records concerning foreclosure, receivership or financial distress; and
- underwriting performed in connection with a proposed transfer or refinancing.

Format and processing:

Please provide responsive records electronically.

For spreadsheets, databases or tabular records, I request the original Excel, CSV or other machine-readable format where available rather than a PDF printout.

For email, please include attachments and sufficient header information to identify the sender, recipient and date.

If portions of a record are exempt, please redact only the exempt information and disclose all reasonably segregable portions. Please identify the statutory basis for each withholding or redaction.

If estimated fees will exceed $50, please provide an itemized estimate before incurring the charge.

If MSHDA believes this request would be significantly less burdensome if processed in stages, I am willing to prioritize the records in the following order:

1. Original applications and tenant-homeownership/disposition commitments
2. Transfer and ownership-change records
3. Forms 8609 and regulatory/extended-use agreements 
4. Compliance records
5. Financial records

Please contact me before excluding potentially responsive records on the basis of scope so that I may clarify or narrow the request.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

title: Flock Safety Contract - Smith County Texas

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Flock Safety Contract - Smith County Texas
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

A copy of any Contract, Agreement, or Memorandum of Understanding between any Department and Flock Group Inc. (DBA Flock Safety).

Excluded from this request:

Confidential information deemed protected by Texas Law, Statute or Attorney General Ruling.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Harry Sisson
